answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with quadratic stake: every identity posts a slashable bond, and voting weight grows only as the square root of that stake, so splitting capital across accounts dilutes rather than multiplies power. To gain influence an attacker must mint a ripple of fresh identities, each demanding its own bond; each delta of stake moved elsewhere yields sharply diminishing returns, while a public atlas links every identity to its collateral. Ten times the votes cost far more than ten times the stake, and detected fraud slashes the whole pool.
